options.title: Monitor bed occupancy and physician pace
options.description: Track bed occupancy and physician pace during high-demand periods to understand the root causes of delays.
options.local_fit: No library evidence, but this option aligns with the observed pattern of long room-to-physician times.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If bed occupancy remains high and physician pace lags, pressure might shift back to the Charge Nurse and Physician Lead to explore further capacity-building measures.
options.how_we_would_know: By monitoring bed occupancy and physician pace over a specified period, we can gain insights into the factors contributing to the observed delays.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If bed occupancy decreases and physician pace improves, indicating successful capacity management, this monitoring option can be discontinued.

options.title: Review staffing levels and patient acuity
options.description: Examine staffing levels and patient acuity during the specified time window to identify potential gaps that might have impacted physician pace.
options.local_fit: No library evidence, but this option addresses the possibility of staffing or patient acuity changes impacting the physician's ability to keep up with rooming rates.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If staffing levels or patient acuity were indeed factors, pressure might shift to the Charge Nurse and Physician Lead to adjust staffing plans or patient management strategies accordingly.
options.how_we_would_know: By reviewing staffing levels and patient acuity data, we can determine if these factors played a role in the observed delays.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If staffing levels and patient acuity were not significant factors, this review can be discontinued, and other potential causes can be explored.

recommendation.rationale: Monitoring bed occupancy and physician pace provides a direct insight into the root causes of the observed delays. This option is recommended as it offers a targeted approach to understanding the specific challenges faced during high-demand periods.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the monitoring reveals that bed occupancy is not a significant factor, or if physician pace is found to be adequate, the focus might shift to exploring other potential causes, such as patient triage or rooming processes.

suggested_reviewers.why: The Charge Nurse is responsible for managing bed occupancy and has insights into physician workload, making them well-positioned to provide context and insights into the observed delays.
The Physician Lead oversees physician staffing and workflow, and can offer valuable perspectives on physician pace and capacity management.
